questions.prompt: Decide whether \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&3\\0&1&-2\end{pmatrix}\) is in reduced row echelon form.
questions.answer: Each non-zero row has a leading 1. The leading 1 in column 1 has zeros above and below it, and the leading 1 in column 2 has zeros above and below it. The pivots move right down the rows. Therefore the matrix is in reduced row echelon form.

questions.prompt: Explain why \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\0&1&4\end{pmatrix}\) is not in reduced row echelon form.
questions.answer: The matrix is in echelon form, and each pivot is 1. However, the pivot in column 2 has a non-zero entry above it: the 2 in row 1 column 2. In reduced row echelon form, each pivot column must have zeros everywhere except at the pivot. Therefore the matrix is not in reduced row echelon form.

questions.prompt: Reduce \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2&5\\0&1&3\end{pmatrix}\) to reduced row echelon form.
questions.answer: The second row already has pivot 1 in column 2. Eliminate the 2 above it using \(\mathbb R^1\) <- \(\mathbb R^1\) - 2R2. Compute \((1,2,5)\) - 2\((0,1,3)\) = \((1,0,-1)\). Keep \(\mathbb R^2\) as \((0,1,3)\). The reduced row echelon form is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&-1\\0&1&3\end{pmatrix}\).

questions.prompt: Read the solution from the RREF augmented matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&4\\0&1&-7\end{pmatrix}\).
questions.answer: The first row represents \(x=4\). The second row represents \(y=-7\). Therefore the solution is \((x, y)\) = \((4, -7)\).

questions.prompt: Reduce \(\begin{pmatrix}2&0&6\\0&3&12\end{pmatrix}\) to reduced row echelon form.
questions.answer: Scale the first row by 1/2 to get \((1,0,3)\). Scale the second row by 1/3 to get \((0,1,4)\). There are already zeros above and below the pivots. Therefore the RREF is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&3\\0&1&4\end{pmatrix}\).

questions.prompt: For RREF matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2&5\\0&1&-1&3\end{pmatrix}\), write the solution set using free variable \(z=t\).
questions.answer: The rows represent x + 2z = 5 and y - \(z=3\). Let \(z=t\). Then \(x=5\) - 2t and \(y=3\) + t. Therefore the solution set is \((x, y, z)\) = \((5 - 2t, 3 + t, t)\), where t is any real number.

questions.prompt: Determine whether \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}\) is the RREF of a consistent system in variables x and y.
questions.answer: The second row represents 0x + 0y = 1. This is impossible. A row of the form [0, 0, non-zero] means the system is inconsistent. Therefore it cannot be the RREF of a consistent system.

questions.prompt: Reduce \(\begin{pmatrix}1&1&4\\1&-1&0\end{pmatrix}\) to reduced row echelon form.
questions.answer: Use \(\mathbb R^2\) <- \(\mathbb R^2\) - \(\mathbb R^1\) to get \(\mathbb R^2\) = \((0,-2,-4)\). Scale \(\mathbb R^2\) by -1/2 to get \((0,1,2)\). Now eliminate the 1 above the pivot in column 2 using \(\mathbb R^1\) <- \(\mathbb R^1\) - \(\mathbb R^2\): \((1,1,4)\) - \((0,1,2)\) = \((1,0,2)\). Therefore the RREF is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2\\0&1&2\end{pmatrix}\).

questions.prompt: Identify pivot columns and free columns in \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&3&0\\0&1&-2&0\end{pmatrix}\). Treat the last column as a constants column.
questions.answer: Ignoring the constants column, the coefficient columns are 1, 2, and 3. The leading 1s are in columns 1 and 2, so those are pivot columns. Column 3 has no pivot, so it is a free column. Therefore variables x and y are pivot variables, and z is free.

questions.prompt: A learner says echelon form and reduced row echelon form are the same. Give a counterexample and explain.
questions.answer: The matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\0&1&4\end{pmatrix}\) is in echelon form because the pivots move to the right down the rows. But it is not in reduced row echelon form because the pivot in column 2 has a non-zero entry above it, namely 2. Reduced row echelon form requires each pivot column to have zeros everywhere except the pivot. Therefore echelon form and reduced row echelon form are not the same.
